blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics, tuned for Medical Devices & MedTech: sector-specific design decisions, the delivery pattern with named owners, and outcomes gated on signed metrics.

MedTech sells outcomes and must prove them: connected devices generate telemetry that feeds service revenue, clinical evidence and regulatory post-market surveillance. The device-to-evidence loop is an engineering product — and EU MDR/CRA raise its bar.

items: Installed base lacks provisioning/OTA; service runs on reactive dispatch and field guesswork.
MDR vigilance and performance data assembled manually; signal detection late.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Industrial IoT & sensor network, Computer Vision & Edge AI, Connected Products & Smart Devices from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Device provisioning/OTA, Service dispatch, Vigilance reporting) on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — EU MDR among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Robots into workflows: AMRs, cobots and autonomous vehicles integrated with safety and orchestration.
Your product becomes a service: device fleets, OTA and telemetry products with revenue attached.
Provisioning, OTA and telemetry for installed base (service moves predictive)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Healthcare & Life Sciences level this capability reads as: infusion pumps, imaging and mobile assets tracked with telemetry and maintenance prediction (asset uptime and utilization up). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability, and it does not flex by account. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
